column2: Dr. and Mrs. Herbert Miller leave for Philadelphia and other Eastern cities
Story by Mendez Marks in The New Yorker
Dorothy Mattison leaves with Boyd and Lind to spend several months with her parents in Springfield (Missouri)
Oliver Freud starts as Assistant Professor of mathematics and physics (Army Specialized Training Program) at the College of William and Mary
Fire: the Service Building is destroyed (upper floor collapsed into the ground floor, rear completely gutted); the fire flares up again around 12:30 after the firemen have left
Expected arrival of Jean Charlot, artist in residence at the University of Georgia, with his wife and their two children
Expected arrival of Dr. Arthur Morgan, former president of Antioch College, and his wife
Marriage of Lieutenant Bela Martin and Virginia Allison
Departure of Radiana Pazmor (for Trion) and of Mr. and Mrs. Eric Werner (for Cincinnati)
Jean Charlot exhibition, open to the public every afternoon (and Tuesday and Friday evenings after 7:30)
Farm: the silo, settled by nine feet, is filled again
Visit by Corporal John Evarts to Lake Eden (September 8-11)
Sam Brown leaves for New England for medical treatment
Farm: a third of the soybean hay cut and set out to dry; the crew works by moonlight until 11 p.m.
Marriage of Aurora Cassotta and Bruno Piscitello
Betty Brett leaves for New York to take her graduation oral examinations
Edward Lowinsky receives his induction order for September 15
Betty Brett's graduation oral examinations under the direction of Jacques Barzun
Additional session of the Textile Workers Union convention at Lake Eden (September 17-26)
Kenneth and Ann Kurtz leave for a ten-day vacation in Wilmington (North Carolina)
Barbara Payne and Marilyn Bauer expected back (Thursday or Friday)
The whole community cleans rooms and grounds and prepares the lodges for the new students, before the textile unionists have all left
The session's first Newsletter goes to press (ready at the end of the week)
A carload of 50 tons of furnace coal, arriving that week, unloaded within the 48-hour limit
Visit by Lawrence Lieberfeld, naval architect
Herbert Miller speaks at the Asheville Rotary Club luncheon: “Contemporary Trends”
Arrival of Clark Foreman, appointed to the faculty, and his family (apartment in the Meadows Inn)
Sam Brown returns to the college
Dr. Straus addresses the staff of the Boston Psychopathic Hospital, at the invitation of Dr. H. C. Solomon (Harvard Medical School)
Arrival of Clark Foreman
Gisela Kronenberg files her application for American citizenship
Josef Albers leaves for Greensboro (Founders' Day at the Woman's College); back Wednesday
Visit by Paul Greer, farm news editor of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch
Larry Fox leaves for New York ahead of his physical examination and induction
Larry Fox called for his army physical
Gisela Kronenberg becomes a research assistant at the Illinois Neuropsychiatric Institute
Erik Haugaard, a future Royal Canadian Air Force pilot, arrives for a visit of several days
John Edsall and Jeffries Wyman, professors of biology at Harvard, visit the college
Fernando Leon arrives for a short visit
Birth of Jeremie Barbara, daughter of Corporal Leo Greene and Hyalie Yamins Greene
Penley, the farmer, on his annual week's vacation (boar hunting)
Two government experts expected to demonstrate the cutting and trimming of mica
Jim Stranch visited by his father (Saturday evening and part of Sunday)
William Morse Cole arrives at Lake Eden for the annual audit of the college's accounts
Dr. F. J. Hansgirg announces to the Board of Fellows a planned gift: a small company to exploit his process for extracting magnesium from olivine, for the future security of the college
Master Sergeant Kedric Lynch, Patsy Lynch's brother, visiting (from Statesboro, Georgia)
F. J. Hansgirg presents the planned gift to the whole community
Private Toshie Kumabe, Bob Kumabe's brother, passing through between New York and Camp Shelby (Mississippi)
Mr. and Mrs. John Christian leave for Washington after a week's visit
Don Page (class of 1943) completes the Army Air Forces Officer Candidate School and is commissioned a second lieutenant

Work program: $50 of mica trimmed and inspected (against $70 of expenses a week); second music cabin nearly finished; three loads of coal carried to the houses; trees felled at the farm while waiting for the coal car; firefighting

Executive committee of the North Carolina College Conference: BMC approved and placed on the “Governor's List” of institutions receiving federal aid for veterans' education (“approved” does not mean “accredited”)
A small fire at the edge of the college dump, quickly put out (more than a hundred hours of firefighting work during the week)
Lieutenant Morris Simon visits Lake Eden for the weekend
Morris Simon goes back to Fort Bragg
Eric Bentley: lecture on Oscar Wilde for the cultural history course and the cast of “The Importance of Being Earnest”; visitors welcome

Work program: pressure tank installed in the chemistry laboratory; nearly 15 pounds of mica trimmed despite the holiday; cow stalls; kitchen–dining hall door soundproofed (Masonite); the coal car for the furnaces arrives, unloaded by morning and afternoon crews
Second Lieutenant Roman F. Maciejczyk, a navigator, dies with eight airmen in a bomber crash near Wendover Field

Thanksgiving: at 6 p.m. the community, “teddibly gay sophisticates,” gathers in the North Lodge lobby, then moves at 6:30 to the “Rhododendron Roof” (dining hall decorated with rhododendrons and felt figures) for dinner and dancing
Marriage of Lieutenant Bedford Thurman to a young woman from Lubbock
Herbert Miller leaves for Boston, where he speaks at the Massachusetts State Conference for Social Welfare

Work program: new tunnel at the mica mine (only ten pounds trimmed); roof of the second cabin finished; hog fence, pigpens moved to the new pens; dining hall stage prepared for “The Importance of Being Earnest”
Lieutenant Don Page arrives for a visit of several days at Lake Eden
Funeral of Roman Maciejczyk, attended by a young pilot who escorted the body
Annual student election: Gwendolyn Currier, a music student, elected moderator for 1944, succeeding Sam Brown
Sergeant John Stix comes back for twenty-four hours
Herbert Miller returns to Lake Eden
Henry Adams begins his classes at Fort Benning (A.S.T.P.)
Each teacher gives Arlyn McKenna a report on each student's work in his or her fall courses; the advisers will summarize them for their students
Election of student officers for the rest of the 1943-44 year
A carload of stoker coal expected “any day”: quick unloading planned
Corporal John Evarts spends half a day in Philadelphia at Morton Steinau's, on his way from New York
Junelaine Smith arrives at Lake Eden for the holidays
Time publishes the article “Black Mountain's Tenth” in its Education section
Edward and Gretel Lowinsky arrive at Lake Eden with their daughter Naomi Ruth
Black Mountain New Year's Eve party at the Jamiesons' in Boston (the Babcocks, Nancy Russ, Nan Oldenburg, Jimmie Jamieson, Jim Raymond, Sam Brown, the Wrights, Mimi French, Ati Gropius)
Richard Davis-Smith (Washington) arrives to visit Ted Hines
Mr. and Mrs. George Thorp (Chicago) visit the Lowinskys for the weekend; Thorp directed the Quaker refugee projects in Iowa for two years
Holly Gregory leaves by train for Massachusetts; she will not return in January
Kenneth Kurtz leaves for a two-week vacation in Florida
Junelaine Smith goes back to New Orleans
Corporal Wille von Moltke, an apprentice teacher in the art department in fall 1940, arrives for twenty-four hours
The Board of Fellows announces the appointment of Jean Charlot to the faculty for the summer quarter 1944
Quintus Dreier leaves for Putney School (Vermont), where he has won a scholarship
Start-of-term work program: four days of thorough cleaning (lodges, dining hall, Studies Building, grounds); digging and grading under the science laboratory extension (Bas Allen); six loads of coal
Dick Bush-Brown returns to the college for the winter quarter
Square dances: Pete Hill calls the figures
Sudden death of Janie, the youngest child of Bill and Martha McCleery
Corporal Pete Hill, on a twelve-day furlough from Camp Gordon Johnston, visits for the weekend

Work program: ears of corn brought in from Grove Stone Field; slab for the magnesium plant extension; land clearing; hauling coal, sand, and gravel; three pounds of mica; cement walk in front of the Studies Building; rented field across the river cleared and plowed for the first time
Pete Hill leaves for Philadelphia (at Marten and Barbara Steinau's), then Boston
The January newsletter goes to the printer; mailing planned for the following Tuesday

Student and faculty concert: Vivaldi, double concerto in D minor (Trudi Straus, Gretel and Edward Lowinsky); Bach, three preludes and fugues from the Well-Tempered Clavier II (E. Lowinsky); Schubert, sonata in A minor op. 164 (Frederic Cohen); Beethoven, trio op. 1 in D major (Straus, Gwendolyn Currier, Cohen); soldiers from the Weather Ring among the guests
Kenneth and Ann Kurtz return from Baltimore, where Ann was examined and treated at Johns Hopkins

Work program: wood cutting well organized, the miners switch to wood because of the danger in the mine; six pounds of mica; cornstalks carried to the farm; magnesium plant (grading, cement, painting); earth from the excavation carried under the Studies Building
The Asheville Citizen publishes Ted Dreier's letter “An Opinion As To The Necessity of a National Service Act,” with an editorial commenting on it
Charles Lindsley, former professor of chemistry, arrives with his young son for three days at Lake Eden
Discipline Committee: visits to the Studies Building by people from outside the community
Faculty: continued discussion of winter quarter registrations
Herbert Miller and students at the parent-teacher association meeting of the Black school in Black Mountain: talk on “Education and Social Problems”
